maria: heads up — after the kernel-selection/graph-capture change in staging we saw a regression on multi-gpu runs. p50 latency doubled for long sequences. suspecting capture+event ordering with our KV prefetch stream.

maria: repro timeline: deploy at 11:02, nightly perf job (8-GPU) shows one rank stuck waiting on all-reduce, others compute fine. overall throughput drops ~2.1x.

deploy-bot: [deploy] service/redwood-runtime v2.7.4 rolled to staging by ci/cd at 2026-03-17T11:02:05Z :rocket:

ben: can you paste the minimal trace/profile? nvprof/ncu timeline or traces from perf-ui would help. also which cudaGraph mode are we using (thread-local vs global capture)?

maria: quick snippet from the nsight timeline (condensed):
```
GPU0: kernel_A (2.1ms) -> cudaGraphLaunch (captured) -> idle 4.8ms -> all-reduce (5.9ms)
GPU1: kernel_B (2.0ms) -> cudaGraphLaunch -> all-reduce (5.9ms)
```
Note: GPU0 shows kernel_A finishes but then idle before all-reduce, while GPU1 goes straight into all-reduce. idle on GPU0 correlates with a cudaEvent recorded from kv-prefetch stream that seems to be waited on inside the capture.

sam: I think this is the classic "event recorded during capture becomes a dependency that serializes across streams" case. If we record an event on stream S_prefetch then do cudaStreamWaitEvent(prefetch_stream, event) inside a capture or graph, capture will bake in the wait as a host-driven dependency. That prevents overlap.

anya: yes. our kernel-selection change moved kv-prefetch to a separate stream and we attempted to capture both compute and prefetch into the same graph. CUDA graph capture semantics don't allow implicit cross-stream dependencies the way we expect — they often turn into host-syncs or serialize the launch order.

maria: exact code where we capture (simplified):
```
cudaStreamBeginCapture(compute_stream, cudaStreamCaptureModeGlobal);
// enqueue compute kernels
kv_prefetch_async(prefetch_stream, ...); // records events into prefetch_stream
cudaStreamWaitEvent(compute_stream, prefetch_event, 0);
cudaStreamEndCapture(compute_stream, &graph);
cudaGraphInstantiate(&instance, graph, ...);
cudaGraphLaunch(instance, compute_stream);
```
This used to work when prefetch was on the same stream. moving prefetch to other stream + capture changed the semantics.

ben: do we record the event before capture starts or during capture? If event is recorded during capture on a different stream, capture may inject a host node or serialize.

maria: event is recorded during capture window — that's the diff. before change, prefetch was on compute_stream so no cross-stream wait needed.

sam: quick mitigation we tried: move prefetch outside of capture (do not record it while capturing), then manually insert a cudaGraphHostNode or a graph-level wait after instantiation. That made overlap reappear in the profiler.

anya: other options:
- keep prefetch on a dedicated stream but record event before BeginCapture (i.e., pre-warm prefetch), or
- avoid cudaStreamWaitEvent inside capture — use graph nodes that express dependency instead (cudaGraphAddDependencies, or capture both streams together with cudaStreamCaptureModeGlobal and ensure proper ordering), or
- skip capturing the prefetch ops entirely and launch them asynchronously per step.

ben: can you try the fast repro: run 2 GPUs with batch size 4, model shard across TP, run kernel-selection branch and capture-as-is vs capture-with-prefetch-outside. attach ncu timeline. I can triage after.

maria: running now. quick note from the live run: when capture includes the wait, NVTX shows a long host-bridge marker (~6ms) at the point of the wait. launch serialization visible.

sam: interesting — also check NCCL usage: if NCCL calls are inside captured graph they may be scheduled differently. NCCL uses CUDA launches that expect certain stream ordering; capturing them can change progress if there are implicit host-driven synchronizations. Did we accidentally capture an all-reduce inside a graph where ranks don't match events?

maria: NCCL ops are launched after graph launch, not captured. all-reduce is outside — but the serialization of compute->all-reduce still happens because the graph inserted the wait. so even though NCCL is outside, it can't overlap because the device is idle waiting on that recorded event dependency.

anya: TL;DR: capture+cross-stream event wait => graph serialized waiting for a prefetch that was meant to overlap. Plan: revert kv-prefetch stream move in the kernel-selection patch, or change capture boundaries to exclude prefetch. We'll also add a unit perf test that runs small 2-gpu job capturing and asserts overlap (compute and comm overlap metric).

maria: I'll open a revert PR for the kernel-selection change to unbreak staging, plus a follow-up to rework capture boundaries.

ben: please include the ncu timeline and the small reproducer script in the PR. also add a short comment linking to this thread.

maria: will do. thanks everyone. :pray:

deploy-bot: [ci] mariak/revert/graph-capture-prefetch added by maria — CI started :white_check_mark:
